Raily Keyring

Build it, flash it, press it.

What's in the box

XIAO nRF52840 Sense, pre‑soldered
Expansion Board
Haptic motor DA7280
Grove-Qwiic hub
Grove cable, 5 cm
Qwiic cable, 50 mm
LiPo battery 602030
USB-C data cable
Printed case
Split ring, 25 mm
M2 × 16 countersunk screws and nuts, 4 each
Double-sided foam tape

No soldering: the XIAO comes with its pins, and every cable plugs in. Parts not to scale.

Raily Keyring2

What you're building

Everything connected on the bench, before it goes into the case.

The pages that follow build it in this order: board, motor, firmware, app, battery, case.

Raily Keyring3

Onto the board

1The XIAO Sense comes with its pins already soldered. There is no soldering in this build.

2Push it into the two inner rows of sockets, all the way down. USB-C at the edge without the screen.

Before the cover goes on, the spring pins under the USB-C end lift the XIAO slightly. That is normal.

Raily Keyring4

Motor and power

3Plug the 5 cm Grove cable into the port marked UART and into the hub. Then the Qwiic cable from the hub into the motor.

Grove and Qwiic plugs fit one way only. On the bench the hub and the motor lie loose; in the case the hub sits on the screen and the motor on its shelf (see «Into the case»).

4Connect USB-C to your computer. No battery yet.

Use a cable that carries data. The battery waits until page 8.

Raily Keyring5

Flash

Open Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and paste:

Flash my Raily Pin using https://github.com/railyai/raily-pin

5Your AI assistant installs the firmware and checks it.

It explains each step and asks before it writes to the board. No assistant? See «Flash by hand» at the back.

Raily Keyring6

Make it yours

6Install the Raily Device app and sign in.

Download link: devices.railyai.com/build.

7Press the button on the board edge. The app binds the keyring to you.

Then tap Pair in the app and confirm on the iPhone: without it, presses do not reach the phone. Test on USB: each press shows up once. The motor starts working with the firmware your agent installs.

Raily Keyring7

Battery

8Check + with a multimeter first.

Red probe on contact A reads +3.9 V: A is plus. A must meet the + printed by the socket. Reads −3.9 V? The red probe is on minus: move it to the other contact and check for +3.9 V.

9Switch OFF, plug in the battery, switch ON.

Red wire to +. Push the plug by its body, never by the wires.

Raily Keyring8

First charge

10Watch the first charge for 30 minutes, outside the case.

Board and battery in a LiPo-safe bag, the USB-C cable in the XIAO. No smell, no swelling, no heat.

Raily Keyring9

Print the case

Skip this page if your kit came with a printed case. Four plates: tray (loop and side button included); shelf; the cover plate: face (LED skin included), frame, dowels and the TEST pieces; and the dowel pusher. The pusher (Ø12 × 40 mm, one cup Ø3.4 × 1.5) is Pastel Periwinkle, like the cover plate: about 2.7 g, about 35 min. Print it once and reuse it for every cover.

V1. Cotton White body, loop and button. Pastel Periwinkle front.

V5. Cotton White body. Pastel Periwinkle front, loop and button.

Polymaker Panchroma Matte PLA, 1.75 mmSKUPer case
Matte Cotton WhiteCA04016about 21 g, with supports
Matte Pastel PeriwinkleCA04036about 20 g, dowels and pusher included
  • V1: every plate is one colour: tray and shelf Cotton White, the cover plate Pastel Periwinkle. No colour changes.
  • V5: the tray changes colour at the loop and the button, so it needs a two-colour printer.
Raily Keyring10

The cover

Test one dowel first: press it into the TEST bar until it stops, then push the TEST plate on. It should hold firmly. Loose, or the plate will not go on? Stop and ask in GitHub Discussions before you assemble.

11Frame face up: press a dowel into each hole 1–9 with the pusher until it stops. It stands about 2.7 mm proud. The plate has spare dowels; keep them.

12Face on: its two locator holes over dowels 2 and 6, loop end to loop end. Press with your palm over each dowel until it sits flat, with no gap at the loop end.

13Turn the cover face down. Slide an M2 nut into the side slot of each of the four pillars until it lines up with the hole: check with a screw tip.

Raily Keyring11

Into the case

Before you start: switch OFF, then unplug the battery, the Grove and the Qwiic cables.

14Battery into its bay, the lead up through the notch toward the board. Never clamp, tape or glue it: it must stay replaceable.

15Shelf onto its ledges over the battery, its arrow toward the loop.

16Motor board onto its seat on the shelf, the round motor up. The ringed socket takes the Qwiic cable.

Raily Keyring12

Board, hub and cover

17Board onto the four standoffs, USB-C in the end window. Plug in the battery lead, switch still OFF.

18Hub onto the board’s screen with a square of foam tape. Grove cable from the UART port into the hub, Qwiic cable from the hub into the motor board.

19Turn the cover face up and set it on the tray: USB-C end first, then press the loop end down until the rim sits flush.

Raily Keyring13

Screws and done

20Turn it over: four M2 × 16 countersunk screws from the back into the pillar nuts. Snug, not tight.

Switch ON with a pen tip through the slot on the other long side. Press the side button to use it. The status light shines through the face near the USB-C end.

21Thread the split ring through the loop.

Raily Keyring14

Important information

Battery polarity

Sellers wire JST-PH plugs differently, so the red wire is not proof. Set the multimeter to V DC and touch the two plug contacts. A positive reading means the red probe is on plus. That contact must line up with the + printed by the board socket. If it does not, stop and do not plug it in. A negative reading means the probes are swapped.

Charging

Buy the 602030 cell only from a seller that provides its UN38.3 test summary. Charge through USB-C from a CE-marked 5 V charger, never unattended, in a bed or in a pocket. Regular charging only after the charge current is confirmed for your board revision and the cell's datasheet; until then, charge only while you watch. Hot, swollen or smelly? Unplug it and let it cool somewhere safe.

Never

  • A battery on the Expansion Board and on the XIAO's battery pads at the same time.
  • A swollen or damaged cell.
  • A clamped, screwed-down, taped or glued cell.
  • A first charge inside the case.
  • Soldering onto the battery.

Using it

Not a toy; keep it from children. Not waterproof. Not an emergency or medical device. At the end of its life, take it to an electrical waste or battery collection point.

Print settings

Polymaker Panchroma Matte PLA, 0.4 mm nozzle; sliced for a Bambu Lab A1 mini. Tray: bottom on the bed, 0.16 mm layers, grid support under the key loop only, about 1 h. Shelf: fence on the bed with a 5 mm brim, 0.16 mm, grid support under the plate and the ledge, about 20 min. Cover plate, no supports, about 1 h 50 min: the face on its flat back at 0.08 mm with the top ironed; the frame parting face down and the dowels standing on their sprue, both at 0.16 mm. Pusher: standing upright, cup end up, 0.16 mm, no supports, about 35 min. Case 49.6 × 89.5 mm, 24.0 mm thick over the front (20.3 at the rim), 97.8 mm long with the loop.

Important information

Flash by hand

Download the firmware and the start-up program update for your board from download.railyai.com/pins (links in the README at github.com/railyai/raily-pin). Check each file’s SHA-256 against releases.json in that repository before you copy it. Press reset twice quickly; a drive appears: XIAO-SENSE on the Sense board, XIAO-BOOT on the plain one. If the first line of INFO_UF2.TXT does not start with «UF2 Bootloader 0.9.2-OTAFIX2.3», copy the update, wait for the drive to return and check again; keep the cable in. Then copy the firmware (.uf2). Full steps: the README at github.com/railyai/raily-pin.

Help

Questions and build photos: GitHub Discussions in railyai/raily-pin. Firmware bugs: Issues in the same repository. Your account: Help in the app. Never post your device ID (it starts with rp1-).
